chunks: Hariz narrated from Muhammad ibn Muslim who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the Ahl al-Zimma (people of the covenant), 'What is upon them from that which preserves their blood and their wealth?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'The Kharaaj (land tax). So if the Jizyah (poll tax) is taken from their heads, then there is no claim upon their land, and if it is taken from their land, then there is no claim upon their heads.'

key_terms.أَهْلِ الذِّمَّةِ: People of the covenant; non-Muslims living under Islamic rule
key_terms.الْجِزْيَةُ: Poll tax; a tax levied on the heads of adult males
key_terms.الْخَرَاجُ: Land tax; a tax levied on agricultural land

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Jizyah and Kharaaj in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiscal principle of mutual exclusivity between the poll tax (Jizyah) on individuals and the land tax (Kharaaj) on property, ensuring non-Muslim subjects are not double-taxed. It reflects the classical Shia juristic view that the security of life and property is contingent upon the specific tax levied, a distinction crucial for understanding the economic rights of Ahl al-Zimma in an Islamic state.
